framework_metadata.title: TARKAX Workflow Diagnostic Framework
framework_metadata.description: A reusable, workflow-agnostic diagnostic framework to evaluate operational workflows across any business function.

dimensions.name: Bottlenecks
dimensions.definition: The degree to which work items accumulate at specific stages due to capacity constraints, approval requirements, or resource starvation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Bottlenecks dictate the maximum throughput of the entire system. Optimizing non-bottleneck steps yields zero systemic improvement.
signals: Resource utilization approaching 100% at specific nodes
metrics: WIP (Work In Progress) to Completion Ratio
example_indicators: Approvals pending for > 48 hours
Single individual responsible for 80% of step execution
failure_patterns: Batch Processing Delays (waiting for end of week/month)

questions.text: What percentage of workflow steps require human approval before proceeding?
How often do tasks sit idle waiting for a specific resource or role to become available?
Is there a single step where work consistently accumulates faster than it can be processed?
How frequently are SLA (Service Level Agreement) deadlines missed due to wait times at a specific stage?
When the volume of work increases by 20%, does the processing time increase exponentially rather than linearly?
How often are 'expedite' or 'rush' requests used to bypass standard queues?
Are there specific individuals whose absence (e.g., vacation, illness) brings the workflow to a halt?
What is the ratio of active processing time to idle wait time for a typical work item?
How often does batching (e.g., waiting for end-of-day processing) cause downstream delays?
Are queues visible to all participants, or are bottlenecks only discovered after deadlines pass?

remediation_suggestions: Implement parallel processing where sequential steps are not strictly required
Introduce auto-approval thresholds for low-risk items
Cross-train staff to alleviate single-resource dependency

dimensions.name: Governance
dimensions.definition: The structural oversight, policy adherence, and standardized operational procedures that regulate how the workflow is executed.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Without governance, workflows degrade into ad-hoc processes, increasing operational risk, inconsistency, and audit failures.
example_indicators: No documented SOPs exist
Decisions are made via untracked Slack/Teams messages

questions.text: Is there a clearly documented, up-to-date Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for this workflow?
Is there a designated single point of accountability (owner) for the end-to-end workflow?
How frequently are exceptions to standard policy requested and granted?
Are all workflow modifications or updates formally reviewed and approved before implementation?
How often are steps executed differently depending on which individual is assigned?
Is there a defined escalation matrix for when edge cases or disputes occur?
Are historical records of workflow execution maintained and easily accessible for audit purposes?
Do participants receive formal training and certification before executing critical workflow steps?
Are the operational limits and authority thresholds explicitly defined for all roles?
How often is the workflow periodically reviewed for alignment with current business objectives?

remediation_suggestions: Establish a formal RACI matrix
Digitize and version-control SOPs
Implement enforced decision gates with audit logging

dimensions.name: Automation
dimensions.definition: The extent to which programmatic systems execute workflow steps without human intervention.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Automation drives scalability, reduces human error, and lowers per-transaction operational costs.
signals: High volume of manual data entry
example_indicators: Staff spend >2 hours daily manually syncing data
Triggers are manual rather than event-driven

questions.text: What percentage of the workflow's data entry involves manual typing or copy-pasting between systems?
Are workflow triggers event-driven (e.g., system alert) or manual (e.g., someone sending an email)?
How often do humans perform deterministic tasks that follow rigid IF/THEN rules without requiring judgment?
Is data automatically validated upon entry, or does it require manual review for correctness?
What is the Straight-Through Processing (STP) rate where a task completes with zero human touch?
Are status updates and notifications generated automatically by the system?
How reliant is the workflow on unmanaged local macros or personal spreadsheets?
Do systems autonomously retrieve necessary enrichment data, or must humans search for it?
How frequently do automated steps fail, requiring manual fallback procedures?
Are documents (e.g., invoices, reports) automatically generated from structured data?

root_causes: Process not standardized enough to automate
remediation_suggestions: Deploy RPA for legacy UI interactions
Implement API-driven data synchronization
Standardize unstructured inputs into structured web forms

dimensions.name: Visibility
dimensions.definition: The degree of transparency into the real-time status, historical performance, and operational state of the workflow.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Without visibility, management operates blindly, making it impossible to proactively address issues or optimize performance.
example_indicators: Status meetings are required just to know where things stand
Tracking relies on a static Excel file updated weekly

questions.text: Can stakeholders view the real-time status of any active item without asking a human?
Are key performance metrics (KPIs) available via a live, automated dashboard?
How much time is spent weekly manually compiling status reports for management?
Is there a clear, auditable trail showing exactly who did what, and when?
When an item is delayed, are automatic alerts triggered, or is it only noticed reactively?
Are performance trends (e.g., throughput over the last 30 days) easily accessible?
Can you immediately identify where an item is stuck and who is responsible for the next step?
Is the underlying data source for reporting a single source of truth (SSOT)?
How often do different teams report conflicting numbers regarding the same workflow?
Are workflow participants aware of their own performance metrics relative to targets?

remediation_suggestions: Implement a unified operational dashboard
Enforce state-change logging in the core system of record
Replace status meetings with automated alert subscriptions

dimensions.name: Handoff Quality
dimensions.definition: The reliability, completeness, and clarity of information transferred between distinct steps, systems, or teams.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Friction at system and human boundaries causes rework, delays, and context loss, severely degrading workflow efficiency.
signals: Ping-ponging of tasks back and forth
example_indicators: Tasks are frequently returned because 'missing information'
Downstream teams have to manually verify upstream data

questions.text: How frequently are tasks rejected or sent back upstream due to missing or incorrect information?
Is there a strict validation gate ensuring all required data is present before a handoff occurs?
When work is handed off, is the full context transferred, or do assignees have to ask for clarification?
Are handoffs standardized via structured forms/APIs, or are they unstructured (e.g., email text)?
How often do downstream systems/teams need to manually reformat data received from upstream?
Is it clear exactly when responsibility shifts from one party to another?
Do cross-functional teams share a common vocabulary for the data being transferred?
How much time elapses between a task being 'completed' by team A and 'started' by team B?
Are handoff failures automatically logged and tracked for root cause analysis?
Is there a Service Level Agreement (SLA) governing the quality and speed of handoffs?

remediation_suggestions: Implement strict entry/exit criteria for workflow stages
Use structured intake forms with mandatory fields
Standardize data schemas across boundaries

dimensions.name: Knowledge Dependency
dimensions.definition: The reliance on tacit, undocumented human knowledge or specialized expertise to execute workflow steps.
dimensions.why_it_matters: High knowledge dependency creates massive operational risk, limiting scale and making the workflow vulnerable to employee turnover.
signals: Only one person knows how to do it
example_indicators: 'Ask Sarah, she's the only one who knows how this works'
New hires take 6 months to become productive

questions.text: How long does it take for a new team member to become fully productive in this workflow?
Are the decision-making rules explicitly documented, or do they rely on 'gut feeling' and experience?
If the primary operator were to leave unexpectedly, could the workflow continue without severe disruption?
How often do undocumented 'workarounds' need to be used to successfully complete tasks?
Is the documentation detailed enough that an adjacent team member could execute the steps accurately?
How frequently is tacit 'tribal knowledge' required to resolve edge cases?
Are training materials systematically updated when the process changes?
Is knowledge centralized in a searchable base, or dispersed across personal notes and emails?
Do complex steps feature contextual guidance (e.g., tooltips, inline help) directly in the tools used?
What is the 'Bus Factor' (number of people who must be incapacitated to halt the workflow)?

remediation_suggestions: Extract tacit knowledge into decision matrices
Implement inline contextual help in applications
Force job rotations to build cross-training

dimensions.name: Compliance
dimensions.definition: The ability of the workflow to consistently adhere to internal policies, external regulations, and security standards.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Non-compliance results in regulatory fines, legal liability, reputational damage, and loss of business operating licenses.
example_indicators: Sensitive data sent via unsecured email
Steps mandating dual-authorization are bypassed

questions.text: Does the workflow natively enforce mandatory regulatory or security checks without human intervention?
Is all sensitive data (PII, PHI, financial) handled in accordance with strict security standards?
Are complete, immutable audit logs generated for all critical actions and data state changes?
How often do operators bypass compliance steps to meet deadlines or throughput goals?
Is access to the workflow tools strictly governed by the Principle of Least Privilege?
Are compliance requirements updated automatically when external regulations change?
Has the workflow ever failed an internal or external compliance audit?
Are approvals cryptographically or systematically verified to prevent 'rubber-stamping'?
Is data retention and deletion handled according to predefined compliance schedules?
Do compliance controls introduce significant friction, or are they seamlessly integrated?

remediation_suggestions: Shift compliance controls 'left' (earlier in the process)
Implement immutable audit trails
Automate data masking and access controls

dimensions.name: Throughput
dimensions.definition: The volume of work successfully completed by the workflow over a specific period, relative to its maximum capacity.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Throughput measures the actual productivity and economic output of the workflow. Low throughput indicates high friction or inefficiency.
example_indicators: It takes 14 days to process a request that requires 2 hours of actual work
The queue is permanently growing

questions.text: What is the average Cycle Time from the initiation of a request to its final completion?
Is the current output volume sufficient to meet business demands without accruing a backlog?
How stable is the throughput day-over-day (is it consistent, or highly volatile)?
Does the system experience frequent periods of 'starvation' where resources have no work to do?
How much does context switching (handling multiple different types of tasks) degrade overall output?
Is the throughput constrained by system performance (e.g., slow software loading times)?
Can throughput be predictably scaled by adding resources linearly?
What percentage of work requires rework, effectively reducing net successful throughput?
Are there specific periods (e.g., end of month) where throughput dramatically drops due to congestion?
How does the actual throughput compare to the theoretical maximum capacity of the workflow?

remediation_suggestions: Implement WIP limits to focus on completion
Optimize database/system response times
Standardize task batching to reduce context switching

dimensions.name: Tool Sprawl / Integration Friction
dimensions.definition: The degree to which a workflow requires context switching across multiple disconnected applications, leading to operational fragmentation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Excessive tooling increases licensing costs, cognitive load, data duplication, and the probability of systemic errors.
signals: Multiple open tabs to do one job
example_indicators: Operators must log into 5 different portals to complete one customer request
Data is manually synced between a CRM and an ERP

questions.text: How many distinct software applications must a user interact with to complete this workflow?
How often must users manually transfer data from one system to another?
Is there a single source of truth for the data, or are there conflicting records across systems?
How frequently do API integrations between these tools fail or silently drop data?
Does navigating between different tool interfaces cause significant cognitive load or delays?
Are users creating shadow IT solutions (e.g., personal databases) to bypass cumbersome tools?
How often is data out of sync across the different platforms used in the workflow?
Is the tooling architecture intentionally designed, or did it evolve ad-hoc over time?
Do users require multiple different credentials to access necessary systems?
How difficult is it to onboard a new user to all the necessary tools for this workflow?

remediation_suggestions: Consolidate overlapping SaaS tools
Implement an Enterprise Service Bus or iPaaS (e.g., Zapier/MuleSoft) for API sync
Build unified frontend interfaces masking complex backends

dimensions.name: Resilience / Exception Handling
dimensions.definition: The capacity of the workflow to gracefully detect, manage, and recover from errors, edge cases, and systemic failures.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Fragile workflows crash completely when encountering unexpected inputs, causing massive disruptions and requiring expensive manual triage.
example_indicators: A single malformed email attachment stops the entire processing pipeline
No clear protocol exists when the primary database is down

questions.text: When an unexpected input or error occurs, does the workflow fail gracefully or crash entirely?
Is there a dedicated, standardized process for managing and resolving exceptions?
Are errors systematically logged and routed to the appropriate team for rapid triage?
Can the workflow automatically retry transient failures (e.g., temporary network timeouts)?
How long does it typically take to identify and resolve a system-level failure affecting the workflow?
If a downstream system goes offline, is data safely queued or permanently lost?
Are 'unhappy paths' (edge cases) explicitly designed and tested, or largely ignored?
Does the system provide clear, actionable error messages to users rather than technical stack traces?
Is there a fallback manual procedure available when critical systems are unavailable?
How frequently do the same types of exceptions recur without underlying root cause resolution?

remediation_suggestions: Implement Dead Letter Queues (DLQs) for failed transactions
Design explicit fallback routing for edge cases
Enhance telemetry and alerting for failure states

dimension_score.description: Calculated by mapping question responses (A-E) to numeric values, summing, and normalizing.

workflow_health_score.description: The weighted average of all dimension scores. Represents the overall operational health of the workflow.

confidence_score.description: Reflects the completeness and reliability of the data used to calculate the scores (e.g., lower if many questions were skipped or answered 'Unknown').

weighting_model.approach: Default equal weighting (10% per dimension), adjustable dynamically based on industry or specific workflow criticality (e.g., Compliance heavily weighted in Finance).

apqc_mapping.description: The framework maps universally across standard APQC categories because it evaluates the structural meta-properties of work (how it flows, fails, and is governed) rather than the domain-specific content.

examples.HR: Onboarding workflow: Bottlenecks (waiting for IT provisioning), Handoff Quality (HR to Manager).
examples.Sales: Quote-to-Cash: Visibility (deal stage tracking), Tool Sprawl (CRM vs CPQ friction).
examples.Marketing: Campaign Launch: Governance (brand approval), Throughput (assets delivered).
examples.IT: Incident Management: Resilience (MTTR), Knowledge Dependency (relying on L3 engineers).

outputs: What-If Scenario Analysis (e.g., Impact of adding 2 FTEs)

pm_review.q1: Is this framework scalable to hundreds of workflows?
pm_review.a1: Yes. It uses a deterministic, rule-based json schema that allows programmatic execution via APIs or LLM pipelines across massive workflow datasets.
pm_review.a2: Yes. By analyzing meta-properties (throughput, friction, visibility) rather than domain specifics (e.g., tax codes), it applies equally to IT and Finance.
pm_review.q3: Does it align with APQC process structures?
pm_review.a3: Yes. It acts as an evaluation layer that sits on top of standard APQC Process Classification Frameworks, assessing the 'health' of the processes mapped within APQC.
pm_review.a4: Subjectivity in survey responses (if humans answer the questions manually) and the assumption that all dimensions carry equal weight by default (which varies by industry).
pm_review.q5: What should be improved before implementation?
pm_review.a5: Establish exact API schemas for how diagnostic data is ingested (e.g., connecting to Zapier/Jira logs automatically rather than relying purely on question-and-answer).
